abstract: Re-entry into proliferation requires rapid expansion of the translational machinery to support cell growth. How cells replenish abundant, long-lived tRNAs remains unclear. Increased RNA polymerase III activity can lead to accumulation of pre-tRNAs without proportional expansion of mature pools, suggesting that transcription alone may be insufficient. Using differentiated HepaRG cells undergoing re-entry into proliferation, we quantified precursor and mature tRNA dynamics. While the total tRNA pool expanded with cell number, mature tRNA abundance per cell remained stable, accompanied by lower precursor-to-mature ratios and accelerated precursor turnover, consistent with enhanced maturation. MYC depletion impaired precursor turnover and compromised maintenance of mature tRNAs and their processing machinery. Across distinct proliferative transitions, the magnitude of per-cell tRNA accumulation paralleled changes in processing-factor mRNA and protein abundance, with both responses dependent on MYC. These findings identify MYC-dependent coordination of tRNA production and maturation as a mechanism supporting the distinct biosynthetic demands of proliferative transitions.
